title: Age Limit to be Eligible for Government Co-funded Assisted Reproductive Technology Procedures
what_it_is: Age Limit to be Eligible for Government Co-funded Assisted Reproductive Technology Procedures

sections.label: Enhanced co-funding for older couples
sections.summary: In January 2020 the scheme was enhanced so couples who attempted AR or IUI before age 40 can use up to two of six co-funded ART cycles at 40 or later.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: In January 2020, the scheme was enhanced to allow couples who have attempted assisted reproduction (AR) or Intra-Uterine Insemination (IUI) procedures before 40 years old to tap on up to two of the six co-funded ART cycles for AR procedures at age 40 or later.

sections.label: IVF live birth success rates
sections.summary: 2018 data show IVF live birth success rates fall from about 23% for women aged 30 to 34 to about 6% at 40 to 44 and 0.6% at 45 and older.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: For IVF, for instance, our latest data, 2018 data, show that the success rate of live births arising from IVF drops from around 23% for women age 30 to 34 years, to around 6% for women age 40 to 44 years; in fact, even further down to 0.6% for women age 45 and older.

sections.label: MediSave withdrawal for ACP
sections.summary: Couples not eligible for co-funding who undergo ACP including ART and IVF can withdraw up to a $15,000 lifetime MediSave limit, with no age cap or cycle limit.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: They are not eligible for the Government co-funding scheme.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: So, for couples who want to go through ACP including ART and IVF, they can withdraw from MediSave up to a lifetime limit of $15,000.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: That does not have any age cap nor limit to the number of cycles.

sections.label: ART co-funding scheme history
sections.summary: The Government co-funding scheme for ART procedures was introduced in 2008 and enhanced in 2013, 2018 and January this year, with criteria updated as clinical evidence allows.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: The fact is that we introduced the Government co-funding scheme for ART procedures in 2008.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: This was in order to reduce the out-of-pocket payment for couples who want to go through ART procedures at our public AR centres, in addition to being able to use their MediSave for these procedures.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: We have, in fact, been enhancing this co-funding scheme since then – in 2013, 2018 and just in January this year – in order to support couples in their parenthood aspirations, including couples who may marry later and still wish to try for a child.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: What we are doing now is to try and strike a balance between encouraging couples to marry and fulfil their parenthood aspirations early and if they have difficulty conceiving naturally, to receive IUI or ART treatment early, versus the need to also support couples who may marry later and wish to have a child.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: We will continue to monitor the clinical evidence and where it is possible and appropriate, we will update the criteria.
